Position Title: Senior Program Manager, MIHR

Position Type: Regular Full-Time

Department: COO's Office (MIHR)

Location: Washington, DC - Hybrid

Salary Range: $85,000 - $110,000 - $136,000 (see note)

Note:
The posted salary range reflects the full range of Corus' Senior Manager pay grade and does not represent the anticipated hiring salary for this position. The target hiring range for the Senior Program Manager is expected to fall between the minimum and midpoint of the pay grade, based on program budget, internal equity and experience.

Corus International provides a competitive, growth-oriented, yet fiscally responsible compensation program. Additionally, Corus provides a comprehensive and competitive employee benefit package to protect our valued and dedicated staff and their families. Our benefits include three medical plan options with comprehensive prescription drug coverage, low-cost dental coverage with 100% paid vision insurance. Corus also provides a generous retirement plan and PTO to include vacation, sick, holiday, parental, jury, international travel, and bereavement leave; employer-sponsored basic life/AD&D insurance; employee wellness incentives, and employee work/life balance and assistance programs.

Position Summary

Corus International is seeking a Senior Program Manager
to serve as a key resource for our U.S. Government funded MOMENTUM Integrated Health Resilience (MIHR) project. MIHR aims to improve maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) and nutrition outcomes in fragile and conflict-affected areas.

This hybrid position is based at our headquarters in Washington, DC,
with in-office days on Tuesdays and Wednesdays each week.

The Senior Program Manager (SPM) functions as a highly visible individual contributor and applies their expertise in managing the project cycle for U.S. Government (USG)-funded global health projects across multiple countries, including Ebola response programming and core operations. The SPM provides programmatic guidance and operational management to ensure program goals, deliverables, and donor requirements are achieved. The SPM collaborates closely with colleagues across MIHR Headquarters and implementing countries to ensure project success.

Working in partnership with the Grants and Compliance team, Finance, MIHR's Senior Technical Director, the MERL team, the Director of Programs, other Program Managers, and Chiefs of Parties in country, the SPM maintains a comprehensive understanding of country contexts, program design, implementation progress, and risk and results.

The SPM may support other projects related to MNCH as new funding becomes available.

Responsibilities

Program Management

Establish and manage project cycle best practices, ensuring compliance with MIHR's Project Management Policies and Procedures and related subaward, procurement, and finance and administration requirements.
Manage project startup processes by coordinating handover across Program Strategy, Business Development, and Grants and Contracts; convening key stakeholders; and supporting project staff recruitment, including job description development and interviews, as needed.
Monitor implementation of the country-level programs by tracking progress against targets and deliverables, identifying and addressing risks and challenges, and ensuring that technical and financial reporting requirements are met. Serve as the primary point of contact for prime and subaward contracts and grant agreements, unless otherwise assigned.
Apply expert knowledge of donor rules and regulations to ensure compliance throughout project start up, implementation, and close out activities, including procurement, budget modifications, and award amendments.
Develop and manage new award/project development, approval, implementation, and close out deadlines and flow process in accordance with MIHR's Project Management Policies and Procedures and relevant donor requirements. Play designated role on in these teams, as assigned.
Collaborate with country staff and MIHR's Headquarter Finance and Grants and Compliance teams to oversee grant funds and subawards, contract, and financial performance. Review budget variances, financial reports, and project spending; monitor spending plans, and work with project teams to ensure effective resource utilization, compliance, and timely corrective action, as needed.
Liaise with MIHR's Grants and Compliance team to provide information or carry out follow-up actions related to sub-recipient management (contracting, reporting, and monitoring).
Monitor implementation of the country level programs, backstopping and participating in regular work planning, reviewing progress toward project targets and deliverables, monitoring expenses vs. budgets, identifying issues that need to be addressed, and implementing adjustments needed.

Core Support and Project Analytics

Manage the development and management of timelines to ensure timely completion of high-level core and country project deliverables, including work plans, quarterly, and annual reports.
Manage the implementation of complex core work plan activities across MIHR-supported countries, ensuring timely completion of deliverables and alignment with approved budgets, work plans, and program objectives.
Provide timely, actionable analysis and insights to the Director, Programs and MIHR's Senior Management Team (SMT) to guide informed decision making, strategic planning, and program performance management.
Maintain the Core Deliverable Dashboard as well as other executive-level reporting tools, ensuring timely integration of monthly and quarterly data from multiple sources. Monitor progress against core and country-level work plans, milestones, and deliverables; identify implementation delays, conduct root cause analyses, and present findings and recommendations to the SMT.
Manage the design and implementation of core and country-level tracking and monitoring tools and processes and manage the workstreams of various teams across MIHR to ensure timely and accurate data entry to closely track core activities, deliverables, and operational efficiencies, including routine tracking and monitoring of the use of Smartsheet to provide up-to-date information and reporting metrics on project deliverables and outputs.
Evaluate existing management tools and processes, seeking feedback from key internal and external stakeholders, as appropriate, for effectiveness and efficiency; refine existing and design new analytical tools, processes, data collection mechanisms, methods of analysis, and visualizations to provide enhanced analytics for tracking of core and country activities, financial spending, project hiring, procurement, and any other key data points that may be needed for SMT decision making.

Data Management, Documentation, And Reporting

Manage project communications with donors through implementation for coordination and reporting purposes.
Manage country teams to prepare high-quality, timely technical and programmatic reports, including bi-weekly reports, quarterly and semiannual reports, newsletters, websites and press releases, for internal audiences as well as donors and Corus constituents.
Ensure data integrity and completeness by maintaining project documentation in electronic databases, including Smartsheets and SharePoint.

Business Development

When requested, serve in a proposal role for relevant country-specific interventions and proposals that are related to their current portfolio and/or technical expertise.

Supervisory

This position has no direct reports.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's with at least seven years' relevant experience managing and implementing international development programs. or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience working with colleagues in a multicultural, multi-linguistic environment.
Experience working with US-based and international partners (NGO/FBO/CBOs, universities and other technical institutions).
Experience successfully managing diverse groups of partners with varying capacities and experience.
Experience managing large-scale, multi-country programs.
Strong working knowledge of USG and other international donor funding mechanisms (including grants, contracts, and cooperative agreements).
Strong knowledge of international development, including humanitarian standards and best practices in health.
Demonstrated ability to manage the coordination of/collaborate on program implementation across multiple teams (between departments, between Headquarters and country offices, etc.).
Excellent communication and influencing skills to communicate effectively and credibly in English, both verbally and in writing.
Demonstrated ability to solve complex technical, managerial, or operational problems in a timely and successful manner.
Critical thinker with a can-do approach to problem solving and demonstrated effective interpersonal skills.
Ability to meet short deadlines with quality deliverables.
Demonstrated ability to adapt to fast-paced environments and work with multinational staff.
Demonstrated versatility and integrity as well as leadership, mentorship, management, organizational, and decision-making skills.
Proficiency in Office 365 applications including Word, Excel, SharePoint, and PowerPoint. Experience with Salesforce a plus.
Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
Ability to influence teams where you might have responsibility but not ultimate authority.
Ability to communicate tactfully and develop positive relationships across teams within the project as well as with external groups (donors, partners).
Must have authorization to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship now or in the future.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree.
Professional proficiency in French.
Experience living and/or working in developing countries.
Experience supporting health programs, including global maternal, child, and newborn health, vaccination, and/or WASH programs, in developing and/or fragile contexts.
Experience with database creation, data analytics, and data visualization preferred; experience with Smartsheets a plus.

Physical And Mental Requirements

The physical requirements that may be needed to execute responsibilities may include bending, standing, and walking, etc.
The mental requirements that are essential to satisfactorily executing the responsibilities outlined in this job description include, but are not limited to: learning new tasks, comprehending, and retaining information, completing tasks independently, effectively communicating verbally and in writing, demonstrating proficiency in using computer software to perform assigned tasks.

Other Duties

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities, duties or responsibilities for the position. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. All positions are required to perform any additional tasks assigned by the supervisor. Global positions that are bound by contracts will not be changed without notice and approval.

Working Conditions, Travel and Environment

Corus has a hybrid work policy, allowing work to be done remotely; two days per week (Tuesday and Wednesday) in the office is required.  The employee must be available to work outside normal office hours or weekends as required.
This position must be able to travel as required for standard domestic and international business purposes. While performing the duties of this job in different locations, the employee may be exposed to precarious settings under high-security risks and/or very basic living conditions and outside weather conditions, as well as to infectious diseases.

As a member of the Corus Family, each employee is expected to:

Foster a work environment where everyone feels valued and included.
Support employees' evaluation and promotion processes based on skills

jobs.description:
WHY UT SOUTHWESTERN?

With over 75 years of excellence in Dallas-Fort Worth, Texas, UT Southwestern is committed to excellence, innovation, teamwork, and compassion. As a world-renowned medical and research center, we strive to provide the best possible care, resources, and benefits for our valued employees. Job Description

Join the HJF Team!

HJF is seeking a Research Assistant II - Biomedical Research
to perform research and/or development in collaboration with others for projects. The Research Assistant provides laboratory and technical support to senior technical and professional staff and solves problems of standard complexity in carrying out research projects in a clinical or laboratory environment.

This position will be in support of the Surgical Critical Care Initiative, USU Department of Surgery. The Surgical Critical Care Initiative (SC2i), funded by the Department of Defense was established in 2013. SC2i is a Uniformed Services University center that leverages legacy information from service members, and critically ill civilian and military patients to develop biomarker-driven clinical decision support tools (CDSTs) with the goal of improving patient clinical outcomes and reducing costs across the injury/disease cycle.

The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine (HJF) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing military medicine. We serve military, medical, academic and government clients by administering, managing and supporting preeminent scientific programs that benefit members of the armed forces and civilians alike. Since its founding in 1983, HJF has served as a vital link between the military medical community and its federal and private partners. HJF's support and administrative capabilities allow military medical researchers and clinicians to maintain their scientific focus and accomplish their research goals.

Responsibilities

Plans and conducts projects and workflows under supervision for clinical research and trial investigations.
Ability to work flexible hours for project completion, including occasional nights and weekends
Performs routine data analysis and verifies and corrects data entry.
Maintains records and documentation regarding assigned research.
Documents current or new procedures or protocols for sample selection, data collection, data processing, and/or statistical estimation.
Ensures adherence to laboratory protocols for sample handling and processing to maintain sample integrity and quality in compliance with GCLP/CAP/CLIA (CLIP) requirements.
Conducts routine quality control tests to ensure the integrity and purity of samples.
Quickly identify and resolve issues with sample collection or analysis that may affect outcomes.
Manages the inventory of laboratory supplies and reagents necessary for sample processing, biobanking, and assays.
Processes and biobanks samples promptly according to established standard operating procedures (SOPs) to maintain integrity and quality for analysis.
May perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned or directed by the supervisor. This may include attendance of and participation in required training for role.

Bachelor's Degree.
Minimum of 3-5 years experience required.

Knowledge of complex laboratory procedures and clinical research lab procedures.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
Extensive work experience and technical skills with immunoassays (i.e., Mesocale Discovery, Luminex, ELISA, or equivalent) and nucleic acid extractions from biospecimens.
Experience working in a clinical research environment is preferred.
Ability to maintain high quality records and documentation.
Ability to meet deadlines of projects in a timely and efficient manner.
Ability to work collaboratively with study teams and cross functional teams.
Good communication and analytical skills.
Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines and regulations.

The Fralin Biomedical Research Institute at VTC in Roanoke, VA, is dedicated to the promotion of health and the prevention and treatment of lifestyle-related disease. The Mishra Laboratory at FBRI is seeking a Research Assistant/Research Tech to support research projects focused on cardiovascular and cardiometabolic disease.

The position is primarily research-focused and will support PI-directed in vitro and in vivo studies. Major responsibilities include mouse colony management and genotyping, assistance with animal experiments and exercise interventions, tissue collection and processing, cell and molecular biology experiments, data collection and analysis, and routine laboratory operations. The successful candidate should be detail-oriented, maintain accurate research records, be able to follow established protocols, and work effectively in a collaborative and fast-paced research environment.

Additional responsibilities include maintaining research equipment and supplies, assisting with experimental coordination, preparing data and figures for presentations and manuscripts, and participating in laboratory meetings. The position provides opportunities to learn additional cardiovascular, molecular, cellular, and physiological research techniques under the direction of the PI.

Lab website: https://fbri.vtc.vt.edu/research/labs/mishra.html

Experience with basic molecular biology and/or cell biology techniques.

Demonstrated communication, interpersonal, analytical, and problem-solving skills with strong attention to detail.
Demonstrated ability to use standard computer software for data organization and analysis.
Ability to work respectfully and collaboratively with laboratory members and to maintain appropriate confidentiality regarding non-public research information.

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience working with mice, including colony management, genotyping, tissue collection, or other animal procedures.

Experience with mammalian cell culture, PCR/qPCR, Western blotting, immunostaining, microscopy, or related molecular and cellular techniques.

new_jobs.title: Truckee PSH - Case Manager
new_jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE
We are more than a nonprofit organization. We are a ministry of service that includes nearly 600 paid professional employees dedicated to helping those we serve. We provide compassionate care today for flourishing communities tomorrow. Founded locally in 1911, VOA Northern California & Northern Nevada is one of the largest providers of social services in the region, delivering a broad range of community-based services that transform lives while meeting immediate needs of families, individuals, veterans, seniors, and youth. In fact, VOA-NCNN provides shelter or housing to over 3,500 men, women, and children every night.

OUR MISSION
VOA puts faith into action by providing compassionate human services to empower individuals and strengthen communities. VOA aspires to create a world in which every person lives a life of emotional, physical, and spiritual well-being, filled with hope across Northern California & Northern Nevada.

PROGRAM AND LOCATION
VOA-NCNN, a Certified Great Place to Work, is recruiting for a full-time, Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) Case Manager to anchor on-site services at Pacific Crest Commons, a new housing community in Truckee, CA. You will support tenants in 10 PSH units funded through No Place Like Home (NPLH). Tenants are adults living with serious mental illness who have experienced homelessness, including chronic homelessness, or are at risk of it. The program is part of VOA's services in the North Lake Tahoe-Truckee region, alongside our Pilot Navigation Center, and is delivered in partnership with Nevada County Behavioral Health (NCBH). This role follows Housing First principles. Housing is never conditioned on treatment, and every service is voluntary. Your success is measured by one thing above all tenants keeping their homes, with a target of 85% or more still housed at 12 months. You'll create and maintain an environment where dignity thrives alongside structure, where participants feel seen as whole people rather than problems to solve. The work schedule is Monday - Friday 830AM - 500PM.

POSITION SUMMARY

This position is responsible for the development of a case management plan to assist PSH participants in developing a greater degree of self-reliance and independence. It will include linking participants to education, employment, budgeting strategies/ money management and addressing any bio, psycho, social issues that may lead to homelessness, criminal behavior, or otherwise non-productive lifestyles. The Case Manager will create and maintain an environment where dignity thrives alongside structure, where participants feel seen as whole people rather than problems to solve. This role follows Housing First principles. Housing is never conditioned on treatment, and every service is voluntary. Success is measured by one thing above all tenants keeping their homes, with a target of 85% or more still housed at 12 months.

OBJECTIVES/ACTIVITIES

Responsible for performing daily work requirements to achieve established objectives of the department such as

Hold a welcome visit with each new tenant in their first week, then complete a strengths and needs assessment.
Build a written, tenant-driven Individualized Service Plan (ISP) within 30 days of move-in, including a Crisis Response Plan. Review it at least every 90 days.
Carry out weekly in-unit check-ins to track ISP goals and unit condition.
Serve as the central hub of each tenant's care team, coordinating internal and external providers.
Use Motivational Interviewing and strength-based, trauma-informed approaches; arrange interpreters as needed.
Maintain positive relationships with program participants, landlords, Volunteers of America staff and all community service agencies.
Create and maintain case management files on each participant which will include personal information, educational and job skills, short-term and long-term plans to become self-sufficient in all areas of his/her life and documentation of participants’ progress and assistance in removing obstacles to set goals.
Provide evaluations of individual clients’ needs to maintain their housing. Document all follow-up and placements.
Provide crisis management as needed and mediate conflicts with fellow participants, community partners and neighbors.
Complete all discharge paperwork in a timely fashion.
Complete budget and housing stabilization plans with participants.
Provide resource information and appropriate case planning specific to any participant who has physical or mental impairment.
Participate in Volunteers of America and outside training sessions.
Perform other reasonably related duties as assigned by the Program Manager.
Conduct monthly house meetings
Arrange of facilitate participant transportation, when needed.

Responsible for assistance with client development, tenancy support, and prevention of protection.

Liaison between clients and community service agencies to meet client needs.
Maintain a list of all available community services and providers.
Assure a safe, non-judgmental environment for the clients.
Maintain positive, professional relationships with clients and staff.
Participate in agency and outside training sessions.
Track and monitor signs of housing instability (late rent, lease violations, neighbor relations, unit condition) and conduct intervention early.
Coach tenants on budgeting, lease terms, unit upkeep, daily routines, meal planning and hygiene, at their own pace.
Help with move-in (utilities, household supplies, orientation), lease renewals and reasonable accommodation requests.
Respond within 1-3 business days to any lease violation or eviction notice with a written stabilization plan.
Meet with property management at least monthly and mediate landlord-tenant and tenant-tenant conflicts.

Pacific Clinics provides 24/7 Mobile Crisis Response services for San Benito County residents. Our team responds with compassion, professionalism, and a person-centered approach to de-escalate crises involving individuals who may be experiencing suicidal thoughts, homicidal thoughts, or grave disability. When appropriate, the team also coordinates access to higher levels of care, including hospitalization and other supportive services, to ensure individuals receive the care they need.

Pacific Clinics is seeking compassionate, motivated professionals to join our Mobile Crisis Response Team serving San Benito County. The Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability works toward a world where humans and nature thrive in concert and in perpetuity. The school has a three-part structure:

Academic departments and programs educate students and create new knowledge across areas of research that are crucial for advancing the long-term prosperity of the planet and people.

The Sustainability Accelerator serves as a launchpad for sustainability solutions, turning innovative ideas into transformative and scalable technologies and policies that will substantially improve the quality of human life and our planet. The Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability is dedicated to creating and supporting a community with the richness of experience and background needed to create solutions that benefit all people, particularly those most affected by environmental damage and climate change. For more information, please click here .

The Accelerator team manages operations, runs our competitive project selection process, and provides resources and support to Stanford faculty and research teams. The Program Manager will play a crucial role in the management of projects in the Planetary Intelligence and Climate Adaptation Flagships.

The Accelerator seeks a candidate with experience in knowledge and project management, with a proven ability to maintain and drive the adoption of crucial business practices, systems, and tools, and foster proactive communication across teams and with external partners. We are looking for someone highly motivated with strong interpersonal and organizational skills, who is comfortable with a dynamic, start-up-like environment, and who knows how to get things done.

Coordinate and monitor Planetary Intelligence and Climate Adaptation projects, ensuring they remain on track and within scope, assessing their strengths and weaknesses, anticipating evolving needs, mobilizing the right support, tracking performance and impact, and making recommendations to the Managing Director.
Collect and analyze program data, generate reports, identify trends, prepare presentations and memos, and develop actionable recommendations to drive continuous improvement.

Facilitate communication and identify synergies between cohort projects and external stakeholders.
Represent the Accelerator internally and externally, including at conferences and working group meetings.
Direct project work of the administrative staff assigned to the Planetary Intelligence and Climate Adaptation program.
Serve as a primary operational point of contact for assigned projects and stakeholders, building strong relationships while coordinating communications, resources, meetings, and collaborative activities across Stanford and external partners.
Lead day-to-day program management for complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives, coordinating meetings, timelines, deliverables, communications, and follow-up actions to ensure projects progress efficiently.

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

This position has been deemed critical by the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability Dean’s Office and is exempt from the hiring pause.

This position is based on Stanford’s main campus with consideration given to the option for a hybrid work schedule (partially onsite and offsite), subject to operational need. Interested candidates must include a resume and cover letter to be considered for this position.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment VISA.

About Us

The Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability strives to create a future when humans and nature thrive in concert and in perpetuity. The school is made up of a three-part structure to drive global impact: Our academic departments and programs educate students and create new knowledge across areas of research that are crucial for advancing the long-term prosperity of the planet and people; Institutes bridge scholarship at Stanford and beyond, bringing multiple viewpoints to bear on urgent challenges; The Sustainability Accelerator drives new policy and technology solutions through a worldwide network of partners who work with our teams to develop solutions at a global scale. The school is dedicated to creating and supporting a community with the richness of experience and background needed to create solutions that benefit all people, particularly those most affected by environmental damage and climate change.

For more information on the school, click here .

Precourt Institute for Energy

As part of the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability , the Precourt Institute for Energy concentrates the talents of the University on energy research and education, from basic science and technology to policy and business. Our mission is to spark the creativity, collaboration, learning, and leadership needed for the global energy transformation. The initiatives, research centers, and educational programs of the Precourt Institute connect across campus in all seven of Stanford’s schools supporting work with the potential to solve the toughest energy challenges from science and engineering to policy and economics. We also build collaborations globally with industry, other research institutions, government, and civic organizations in pursuit of sustainable, affordable, secure energy for all people.

Energy Equity & Just Transitions, a program area initiated at Precourt Institute for Energy, aims to:

Integrate the tenets of energy equity into energy education and research at Stanford
Create experiential learning and research opportunities that engage external partners in accountable, collaborative ways to explore and scale pathways to more just transitions
Collaborate with the Explore Energy program based in the Precourt Institute for Energy to propel student and alumni interests in integrating energy equity and just transitions into their professional preparation and career development

Seeking Program Manager, Energy Equity & Just Transitions

Stanford’s Precourt Institute for Energy seeks exceptional candidates to serve as Energy Equity & Just Transitions Program Manager to partner with the Energy Equity & Just Transitions Managing Director in developing and implementing strategies for (1) applying the tenets of energy justice in collaboration with external partners and campus partners in co-curricular learning and (2) integrating practices that advance equity and just transitions into programming at the Precourt Institute for Energy, which intersects with all seven Schools at Stanford.

The Program Manager reports to the Managing Director and works closely with them to lead and execute program objectives and expand strategic goals to meet growing demand.

We are seeking a Program Manager who is creative, resourceful, and excited about endeavoring to advance equity and rapid energy transitions at an institution with world-class research, influential thought-leaders in climate science and energy policy, and an unrivaled ecosystem for entrepreneurs.

Responsibilities Include

Design and manage activities that advance program aims in education, research, and organizational development, such as faculty workshops, Institute convenings, summer fellowship trainings, and projects in Stanford’s Living Laboratory for Sustainability;
Student engagement is a big part of this role. The candidate must have an enthusiasm to work with students and be excited about developing strong, lasting connections with them. Knowledge of Stanford University is preferred but not required;
Manage program activities and related action plans in a high-paced work environment and monitor and evaluate programmatic activities per outlined goals and objectives;
Mentor students, connect them to resources and opportunities, and help them chart a path forward based on their interests in advancing energy equity through their pursuits;
Demonstrate subject matter expertise in energy equity concepts and just transitions strategies and apply that knowledge to implement development of co-curricular learning at every level of degree progress, including alumni executive education, and advisory support for research;
Develop a well-cited repository of resources used in program activities and provide recommendations to campus collaborators seeking such resources;
Manage and track program budget and develop budget proposals and reports;
Develop streamlined workflows to manage activities and resources;
Develop and maintain program communications, including content for the program website in coordination with the Communications Director and Web Developer for Precourt Institute for Energy;
Build and nurture relationships across Stanford’s energy ecosystem to connect opportunities to learn about energy equity and to engage it in their work;
Raise awareness and visibility of the program activities, including marketing and outreach to students and campus partners as well as external partners;
Avidly pursue continued learning and stay current with field developments related to program aims and activities;
Collaborate and work together with other program managers at Precourt Institute for Energy, particularly the Explore Energy team;

Demonstrated excellent organizational skills
Demonstrated ability to take initiative and ownership of projects

Entrepreneurial skills for growing a lean program in early-stage development Demonstrated ability to take initiative and ownership of projects.

Precourt Institute for Energy is a teamwork-focused and collaborative work environment. The program manager reports to the Managing Director for Energy Equity & Just Transitions. In addition, the program manager collaborates with colleagues on the Explore Energy team (Precourt’s student engagement program), including monthly meetings and annual offsites. Job Description

Welcome to Land, Buildings & Real Estate

Land, Buildings & Real Estate (LBRE) is the operational core of Stanford University’s physical campus. LBRE constructs and maintains the Stanford campus, where advancements across the academic spectrum are made possible. Our work is founded upon the collective value of dedication, innovation, expertise, teamwork, and continuous improvement. We are committed to serving the university’s academic mission, as well as preserving and enhancing Stanford’s 8,180 acres, and pride ourselves on supporting the teaching and research of the university as “Caretakers of a Legacy."

Approved budgeted annual salary $140,000-$155,000.

Job Purpose

To provide program management and operational support to the Resilience and Emergency Response programs, including Wildfire Resilience, and the Safety, Resilience and Emergency Response (SRER) Director. Under minimal supervision, perform the most complex technical work in a wide range of resilience, emergency response, environmental, health, and safety disciplines to ensure a resilient work environment and to achieve compliance with the university’s resilience standards.

This role requires onsite presence 4 or more days per week.

Core Duties

Serves as the Stanford University Wildfire Resilience Program Manager

Accountable for completing projects as directed by the WFMP Plan and Wildfire Resilience Steering Committee. This includes vegetation management, frequent field visits, community communications, and collaboration with local fire agencies and groups.
Provides leadership and performs work towards the completion and management of the website and annual report.
Manages vendors, contracts, purchase orders, invoices, and access to properties.
Holds re-occurring operations focused meetings with diverse internal stakeholders to drive initiatives forward.
Partners with and manages consultants to ensure proper documentation, project completion, and innovation in methodologies and best practices are utilized.
Ensures safety, environmental, biological, and cultural sensitivities are adhered to by collaborating with Stanford’s Conservation and Archaeological departments.
Performs industry engagement and outreach, research development, and community representation of the Wildfire Resilience Program.

Resilience & Emergency Response: Operations, Planning, Logistics, & Communications

Under general guidance from the SRER Director, serve in an essential leadership and support role in responding to emergencies virtually and/or physically to support emergency operations.
Respond to campus and utility emergencies 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
Issue emergency alerts to internal customers and stakeholders.
Manages and audits emergency response supply inventory.
Monitors weather conditions and communicates National Weather Service Alerts.
Supports response and resilience initiatives including emergency generator operations and management (smart fuel sensors expansion).
Develops detailed documentation including Building Occupant Emergency Action Plans.
Supports safety, resilience and emergency response during large events at the Stanford main campus.
Supports the adoption of enterprise-wide business continuity software.
Supports and executes emergency generator refueling operations
Identifies opportunities to enhance safety and resilience; provides technical proposals identifying solutions to the Safety, Resilience and Emergency Response Steering Committee.

Coordinates Training & Tabletop Exercises

Holds two or more tabletop exercises annually.
Provides two or more training sessions for Everbridge authorized users (LBRE Alerts) annually.
Provides training on Operational Basemap (GIS) usage for emergency response to all Stanford University Department Operations Centers.
Provides training to department staff who assist in emergencies and/or are assigned a role in the Land, Building and Real Estate (LBRE) Department Operations Center.

Leads RER Documentation Efforts

Constantly monitors operations to identify opportunities for additional documentation and record maintenance.
Leads the Emergency Response Manual (ERM) Annual Updates

Supports Facility Director Liaison Initiatives

Coordinates with Energy Operations and other operational groups to stay apprised of work that warrants special communications to facility directors and utility customers.
Reviews and prepares communications to Facility Directors.
Supports outreach and coordination with Facility Directors for Research Resilience and new initiatives.

Preferred Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

Ability to provide tactical and strategic support to complex projects involving multiple stakeholders.
Ability to support a safe working environment and identify hazards during operations for the entire Stanford community and vendors.
Fundamental understanding of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and other mapping tools.
Ability to learn how to operate a power industrial truck (forklift)
Ability to learn how to refuel emergency generators
Aptitude to quickly learn new software such as mass notification tools, GIS, building management systems, and instant messenger applications (Slack).
Advanced computer skills and demonstrated experience with office software and email applications including shared document management software (Google Docs, Sheets and Slides)
Knowledge, experience or background in understanding utility systems (electric, gas, thermal, steam).
Demonstrated success in following through and completing projects.
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Excellent customer service and interpersonal skills.
Ability to prioritize, multi-task and demonstrate flexibility in decision-making.
Ability to take initiative, ownership of projects and build consensus amongst stakeholders.
Ability to routinely and independently exercise sound judgment in making decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS*:

Frequently stand, sit, use a telephone and cell phone, and other hand held tools and devices.
Ability to work outdoors in severe weather conditions such as extreme heat, extreme cold, and poor air quality.
Ability to safely traverse wildland areas and uneven terrain with changing elevations such as hillsides and areas of dense vegetation.

Occasionally kneel, crawl, climb ladders, reach/work above shoulder, twist/bend/stoop/squat, grasp lightly/fine manipulation, grasp forcefully, write by hand, sort and file paperwork or parts, operate foot and/or hand controls, carry, push, and pull objects that weigh 40 pounds or more.

is seeking a Program Manager - Water & Wastewater Infrastructure

This role is ideal for a leader who thrives at the intersection of strategy, governance, and execution, and brings a strong track record supporting medium- to large-scale Capital Improvement Programs (CIPs).

You will serve as a trusted advisor to owners, guiding programs from planning through design and construction, often within diverse delivery models such as progressive design-build.

Lead program management services for water and wastewater capital programs ranging from $50M to $2B+
Lead integrated teams within complex program environments with multiple disciplines and stakeholders
Coordinate with design-builders, contractors, and subconsultants
Serve as Owner’s Advisor/Consultant, supporting procurement, design, and construction phases
Develop and implement Program Management Plans (PMPs) including governance, controls, and reporting frameworks
Establish and oversee program controls (cost, schedule, risk, change management, and performance metrics)
Advise clients on delivery strategy (DBB, CMAR, Design-Build, Progressive Design-Build)

Support funding strategies including SRF/WIFIA and grant applications
Drive continuous improvement in project delivery, digital solutions (including PMIS and collaborative tools), and reporting systems

Job Description

Please note:
We will consider both Hybrid and Remote candidates for this role.

The Digital Accessibility Program Manager serves as the operational and subject matter backbone to the Office of Digital Accessibility’s service delivery. This role owns the day-to-day functioning of the digital accessibility program in managing the service portfolio, conducting accessibility evaluations, ensuring the quality, accuracy, and timeliness of accessibility reviews from team members, engaging directly with campus clients on complex compliance challenges, and tracking program performance. The Digital Accessibility Program Manager reports to the Director for the Office of Digital Accessibility.

The ideal candidate brings both digital accessibility expertise and strong program management skills, serving as a critical bridge between technical staff and Stanford clients by translating findings, balancing competing priorities, and ensuring clients leave every engagement with clear, actionable guidance. They are equally comfortable guiding a campus web team through a remediation roadmap, reviewing an engineer's audit report for accuracy and completeness, and prioritizing and managing competing tasks with concurrent deadlines.

Core Duties

Program Management:

Manage the digital accessibility service intake pipeline by triaging incoming requests, assigning work, tracking progress, and ensuring reviews and consultations are completed on schedule.
Coordinate with Office of Digital Accessibility staff on workload planning, deadline management, and service delivery priorities.
Maintain quality standards for digital accessibility deliverables and consult with digital accessibility engineers on complex findings or edge cases requiring additional interpretation. Ensure findings are presented in a manner that is solution-focused and actionable for both technical and non-technical clients.
Oversee the interpretation, implementation and compliance with digital accessibility standards and regulations. Recommend actions and/or resolve complex issues with institutional partners that span organizational and university boundaries.

Program Evaluation

Evaluate how existing accessibility tools are offered and based on configuration, adoption, and use, if they are meeting program goals or when alternatives should be considered.
Identify trends in accessibility issues across campus and surface insights that inform strategy and resource planning.
In coordination with the Director, track and maintain key performance indicators and program metrics, including service volume, review turnaround times, client satisfaction, remediation outcomes, and compliance trends.

Planning And Analysis

Under supervision of the Director, execute strategic plans for the Office of Digital Accessibility, leveraging subject matter expertise to meet regulatory and technical challenges for digital accessibility.
Design and evolve the digital accessibility service delivery model, determining how core services (e.g., audit intake, remediation consultation, procurement review, training) are structured and delivered to improve client experiences.
Apply a creative mindset and bring the ability to think outside the box to create innovative service offerings.

Client Management

Advise clients on how accessibility requirements should be applied to specific vendor evaluations while balancing the intersection of technical standards, compliance obligations, and institutional constraints.
Support clients on complex compliance requirements, including situations requiring creative or non-standard solutions.
Navigate difficult conversations with stakeholders who are resistant to or overwhelmed by accessibility requirements.
Translate technical remediation findings into actionable guidance for non-technical content owners, developers, and procurement staff.

new_jobs.description:
About Patelco Credit Union

Patelco Credit Union is a not-for-profit credit union with a purpose to build financial health and wellbeing for our members. Since 1936, Patelco has grown from $500 in assets to over $9 billion in assets and is the 7th largest credit union in California with branches throughout Northern California.

We are here for our members throughout all their stages of life. Meeting them with the products and services to help them plan purposefully for their futures and to secure our life-long partnership as their trusted financial advocate. As one team, we are all committed to delivering service, empowering financial literacy, creating products, and providing new technology for our members.

We believe that work should be rewarding, challenging, and enjoyable. We’re dedicated to creating a positive and supportive culture where our team members can thrive. If you’re looking to use your skills and knowledge to make a difference in our members’ lives, Patelco could be the perfect fit for you.

Overview

The Senior Risk & Controls Program Manager serves as the lead subject matter expert within the Second Line of Defense (2LOD) for Risk and Control Assessments (RCSA), Issues Management, and control effectiveness oversight. This role is responsible for designing, enhancing, challenging, and overseeing the organization's operational risk management practices to ensure risks are identified, assessed, mitigated, monitored, and escalated appropriately.

As the most senior individual contributor within the Operational Risk function, this position provides thought leadership, independent challenge, and strategic guidance to business leaders, risk partners, executive management, Internal Audit, and regulators. The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in operational risk frameworks, regulatory expectations, risk assessments, control evaluations, root cause analysis, action plan governance, and issue lifecycle management.

This role plays a critical part in strengthening the organization's risk culture and ensuring risk management practices are sustainable, effective, and aligned with industry leading practices.

Responsibilities

Essential Duties

Serve as the enterprise subject matter expert for Risk and Control Assessments (RCSA), driving the design, implementation, and continuous enhancement of assessment methodologies.
Provide independent challenge and oversight of first line risk assessments, control evaluations, inherent and residual risk ratings, and mitigation strategies.
Evaluate the quality and effectiveness of risk identification processes across business units.
Facilitate and challenge business leaders during risk assessment workshops, ensuring meaningful identification of key operational risks and control gaps.
Establish standards for control design, control effectiveness testing, and risk rating methodologies.
Analyze assessment results to identify emerging risk trends, systemic weaknesses, concentration risks, and opportunities for control enhancements.
Develop meaningful risk metrics, KRIs, KPIs, and reporting dashboards to provide executive management with meaningful insights into the organization's risk profile.
Establish and maintain standards for issue identification, root cause analysis, corrective action development, validation, closure, and sustainability.
Assess the adequacy and effectiveness of corrective actions to ensure sustainable remediation of identified risks and control deficiencies.
Escalate significant risks and overdue remediation activities to senior leadership and governance committees as appropriate.
Support ongoing maturation of the Operational Risk Management Framework and related programs.
Develop and maintain policies, standards, procedures, guidance, and training related to risk assessments and issues management.
Ensure alignment with regulatory expectations, industry best practices, and the organization's risk appetite framework.
Support governance committees through preparation of risk reporting, presentations, and executive-level risk insights.
Review risk events, internal audit findings, compliance observations, examination results, and operational losses to identify control implications.

Functional Competencies

Ability to provide constructive and influential challenge.
Strategic thinking and enterprise perspective.
Exceptional facilitation and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to build trusted partnerships across all levels of the organization.
Strong ownership mindset and accountability.
Sound judgment in complex and ambiguous situations.

Qualifications

10+ years of risk management, operational risk, internal audit, compliance, controls, or related financial services experience.
7+ years of direct experience leading or overseeing Risk and Control Assessments (RCSA) programs and Issues Management frameworks.
Demonstrated experience working within a Second Line of Defense (2LOD) risk function.
Experience implementing or enhancing enterprise RCSA and Issues Management programs.
Extensive knowledge of operational risk management principles, control frameworks, and risk governance practices.
Strong knowledge of issue management lifecycle governance, remediation validation, root cause analysis, and corrective action planning.
Experience presenting risk information to executive leadership, risk committees, and senior stakeholders.

Physical Activities/Requirements

This position is based out of the Dublin HQ office. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice.

Target Base Pay

$120,170 - $150,212/ yr

Compensation At Patelco

Please note that the salary information is a general guideline only. Patelco Credit Union considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate's work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, as well as market and business considerations when extending an offer. new_jobs.description:
Job Description

This position has been deemed critical by the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability Dean’s Office and is exempt from the hiring pause.

This position is a full-time position based on Stanford’s main campus with consideration given to the option for a hybrid work schedule (partially onsite 3 or more days a week), subject to operational need.

Interested candidates must include a resume and cover letter to be considered for this position.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa.

About Us

The Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability strives to create a future when humans and nature thrive in concert and in perpetuity. The school is made up of a three-part structure to drive global impact: Our academic departments and programs educate students and create new knowledge across areas of research that are crucial for advancing the long-term prosperity of the planet and people; Institutes bridge scholarship at Stanford and beyond, bringing multiple viewpoints to bear on urgent challenges; The Sustainability Accelerator drives new policy and technology solutions through a worldwide network of partners who work with our teams to develop solutions at a global scale. The school is dedicated to creating and supporting a community with the richness of experience and background needed to create solutions that benefit all people, particularly those most affected by environmental damage and climate change.

For more information on the school, click here .

The SDSS Sustainability Accelerator (the Sustainability Accelerator) serves as a launchpad for sustainability solutions, turning innovative ideas into transformative and scalable technologies and policies that will substantially improve the quality of human life and our planet. The Sustainability Accelerator is rooted in the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability and works across the University and with external partners to drive solutions from the lab into the world.

The Accelerator is seeking a full-time Program Coordinator to join our operations team and serve as the primary administrative and programmatic partner to four portfolios of faculty research projects (“Flagships”). The role supports two Managing Directors, each responsible for two Flagships, with time allocated roughly evenly between the two portfolios. The role is a member of the Accelerator Operations team, and works in close partnership with the Managing Directors to understand and support the day-to-day needs of their portfolios, while its manager provides overall supervision, workload prioritization, professional development, and coordination across the four Flagships. Success in this role comes from building close, proactive partnerships with the Flagship teams—keeping coordination moving, anticipating project needs, and making it easier for faculty, researchers, and Accelerator staff to do their work.

We care not only about what you have done, but how you work. Administrative experience provides an important foundation, while curiosity, adaptability, and sound judgment will be equally important for success. The strongest candidate will be comfortable with shifting priorities and incomplete information, will look for opportunities to improve processes and reduce unnecessary manual work, and will pick up and apply new tools, including AI and automation tools, to problems that do not yet have a defined process. The research portfolios change as the science and the partnerships change, and the role changes with them.

What We’re Looking For

Curiosity and adaptability above all. Experience is helpful but not the primary requirement; we care more about how quickly you learn, how you handle changing priorities, and how you exercise judgment when information is incomplete.
An entrepreneurial, proactive, and solutions-oriented approach.
Strong interpersonal and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to support team members and external partners with professionalism and empathy even as priorities shift.
Comfort working across four distinct research portfolios at once, managing day-to-day priorities independently and escalating competing demands when needed.
Interest in the substance of the work: sustainability research, and the process of moving it from the lab into policy and practice.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Managing complex calendars with limited consultation; resolving scheduling conflicts; negotiating and managing the needs of individuals or groups requesting time with the Accelerator members, Stanford leadership, and faculty researchers; including running scheduling polls across large groups and time zones.
Support domestic and international business travel by providing policy guidance, coordinating complex logistics when needed, and processing associated travel reimbursements .
Serving as the primary administrative support contact for two Managing Directors and their four flagships of faculty research projects at the Accelerator.
Participate actively in Flagship team meetings: build agendas with Flagship leads, capture decisions and owners, track next steps, and facilitate timely follow-through.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS*:

Constantly perform desk-based computer tasks.
Frequently sitting.
Occasionally stand/walk, reach/work above shoulders, grasp lightly/fine manipulation, grasp forcefully, use a telephone, sort/file paperwork or parts, lift/carry/push/pull objects that weigh up to 10 pounds.
Rarely twist/bend/stoop/squat, kneel/crawl.
- Consistent with its obligations under the law, the University will provide reasonable accommodation to any employee with a disability who requires accommodation to perform the essential functions of the job.

Working Conditions

WORK STANDARDS:

Interpersonal Skills: Demonstrates the ability to work well with Stanford colleagues and clients and with external organizations.
Promote Culture of Safety: Demonstrates commitment to personal responsibility and value for safety; communicates safety concerns; uses and promotes safe behaviors based on training and lessons learned.
Subject to and expected to comply with all applicable University policies and procedures, including but not limited to the personnel policies and other policies found in the University's Administrative Guide, http://adminguide.stanford.edu .

The expected pay range for this position is $83,404 to $97,850 per annum.

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Act on behalf of the supervisor, department manager, or chair in regards to establishing priorities and identifying and resolving problems that are administrative in nature.
Oversee and/or perform duties associated with scheduling, organizing, and operating complex conferences, seminars, and events, including arranging with vendors for services, overseeing the production and distribution of materials, administering logistics, and managing event within budget.
Compose and draft documents and correspondence for presentations, course handouts, grants, conferences, seminars, and reports. Perform substantial editing and fact checking. Create, maintain, modify, and/or ensure accuracy of content in various unit documents, displays, reports, brochures, social media, and/or websites.
Plan and schedule calendar(s) with limited consultation, resolve calendaring conflicts, and arrange travel in compliance with unit, university, and sponsor policies.
Create complex reports and spreadsheets which may utilize specialized software and systems.
Oversee and/or process a variety of complex financial transactions; produce, monitor, and reconcile budget statements; research, identify, and resolve discrepancies. May assist with capital or special equipment requests and/or vendor selection.
Coordinate and monitor routine maintenance services completion. Plan and coordinate office moves and/or minor renovation projects.
May lead staff or supervise day-to-day work of student and/or temporary workers, including scheduling, assigning, and prioritizing workloads, setting appropriate deadlines, reviewing work for quality and timeliness, and providing performance review input.

High school diploma and four years of administrative experience, or combination of education and relevant experience.

About Us

The Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability strives to create a future when humans and nature thrive in concert and in perpetuity. The school is made up of a three-part structure to drive global impact: Our academic departments and programs educate students and create new knowledge across areas of research that are crucial for advancing the long-term prosperity of the planet and people; Institutes bridge scholarship at Stanford and beyond, bringing multiple viewpoints to bear on urgent challenges; The Sustainability Accelerator drives new policy and technology solutions through a worldwide network of partners who work with our teams to develop solutions at a global scale. The school is dedicated to creating and supporting a community with the richness of experience and background needed to create solutions that benefit all people, particularly those most affected by environmental damage and climate change.

For more information on the school, click here .

The Stanford Woods Institute for the Environment works to advance globalsustainability through new knowledge and practical, fair solutions to pressing environmental challenges. As part of the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability, the Woods Institute provides an interdisciplinary research hub for scholars from all seven schools at Stanford. Offering targeted research incentives as well as convening, education, and leadership programs, the Woods Institute supports faculty, researchers, and students as they investigate and advance solutions to critical climate, environment, and sustainability challenges. Working on campus and around the globe, the Woods Institute and its hosted centers and programs combine cutting edge scholarship, diverse partnerships, and deep engagement across sectors and disciplines to advance just, practical solutions for people and the planet.

Better Bricks is a flagship research initiative of the Stanford Center for Human and Planetary Health , based at the Stanford Woods Institute for the Environment and led by Dr. Steve Luby. The initiative brings together an interdisciplinary team of researchers and partners across South Asia to develop, rigorously evaluate, and scale practical solutions that improve both human health and the environment. Initially launched in Bangladesh 14 years ago, Better Bricks focuses on transforming brick manufacturing - one of the region's largest sources of air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions - through evidence-based innovations that reduce emissions, improve air quality, protect health, and strengthen livelihoods. The program is now scaling its Zigzag kiln intervention across Bangladesh, expanding to India, and developing globally applicable approaches for measuring emissions from brick kilns, with the potential to reduce millions of tons of greenhouse gas emissions while improving the health of millions of people.

Better Bricks is seeking a Research and Program Manager who can contribute independently as a scientist while providing operational leadership for a complex, multidisciplinary research portfolio and serving as a strategic partner to the Director, Dr. Steve Luby, to expand and scale this innovative program of research and impact. The successful candidate will oversee the implementation, coordination, and strategic growth of the Better Bricks portfolio, manage key partnerships, contribute scientific and technical expertise, and lead day-to-day operations across multiple projects and collaborators. The ideal candidate has a PhD in environmental health or a related field, significant professional experience working in South Asia - ideally Bangladesh and India - and a deep understanding of the region's research, government, and implementation landscape. They will have demonstrated success managing complex international research programs involving multiple partners and be a collaborative, highly organized manager who thrives in a fast-paced, interdisciplinary environment, is comfortable navigating shifting priorities, and is passionate about translating science into measurable global impact.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Partner with the Director to define strategic research priorities for Better Bricks and translate the program’s vision into action, ensuring alignment across projects, study sites, partners, donor expectations, and teams.
Manage 2-4 large international subawards of over $2 million total to partners in Bangladesh and India. Ensure partner performance, fiscal responsibility, and impact through proactive communication, deliverable tracking, and budget oversight.
Supervise the design and implementation of study protocols, ensure compliance with IRB, data governance, and international regulatory standards.
Oversee scientific operations, including field logistics, procurement, staffing, training, and quality assurance across study sites.
Develop and oversee data management systems to ensure high-quality, consistent, and secure data collection, management, and sharing across multiple study sites and collaborating partners.
Oversee day-to-day program operations, establishing management systems and identifying opportunities for process improvement. Track timelines and deliverables; trouble-shoot and flag issues to the Director if projects are stalled or delayed.
Serve as the primary liaison with Stanford administrative partners at the Center for Human and Planetary Health to proactively advance administrative processes, resolve operational issues, and ensure projects, personnel actions, contracts, payments, and other key activities move forward efficiently.
Maintain program-level budgets, timelines, and deliverables; develop projections, monitor progress and ensure accountability across research teams. Recommend budget adjustments to the Director.
Build and nurture partnerships with government agencies, academic collaborators, NGOs, and community stakeholders to enhance the program’s scientific and policy impact. Organize and lead regular meetings with international project teams.
Lead or contribute to grant writing, fundraising, and donor reporting activities to support the long-term sustainability of the research portfolio.
Draft peer-reviewed publications, technical reports, presentations, webpage language, and public communication materials for both technical and non-technical audiences.
Along with the Director, be a spokesperson for Better Bricks when opportunities arise.
Provide mentorship and professional development to junior researchers and field teams. Supervise student researchers.
Support the implementation of new Better Bricks initiatives, including the development of an Action Lab course, commercialization of carbon credits generated through zigzag kiln emissions reductions, and other innovative efforts that expand the program's scientific, policy, and financial impact.

In addition to the minimum qualifications listed below, our preferred qualifications include:

PhD in environmental science, public health, environmental engineering, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience leading or managing large, multi-site research programs.
Proven ability to translate scientific vision into operational strategy, aligning people, projects, and resources toward shared research goals.
Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills; ability to liaise with the Director and support ongoing needs across research partners, government agencies, and international counterparts.
Strong organizational and leadership skills, including budget oversight, personnel supervision, and cross-functional coordination.
Strong quantitative and analytical background, with some experience in epidemiologic, environmental, or statistical modeling.
Experience developing and overseeing research study designs, protocols, and compliance documentation (e.g., IRB, data use agreements).
Demonstrated success in grant writing, report preparation, and scientific communication for both technical and non-technical audiences.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and other research management tools for documentation, planning, and presentations.
South Asian language proficiency – ideally Bengali, Hindi, or Urdu.

Core Competencies

Strategic planning and research program leadership
Operational and project management excellence
Stakeholder engagement and cross-sector collaboration
Scientific and analytical acumen (environmental health, epidemiology, exposure science)
Strong written, verbal, and data communication skills

Job Description

The Department of Biomedical Data Science at Stanford University, a premier research-intensive intuition is actively recruiting for a dynamic candidate to serve as a Bioinformatician at 100% FTE in the Julia Salzman lab. The Salzman lab uses experimental and statistical tools to construct a high dimensional picture of human, plant and microbial genome and gene regulation statistical analysis of metagenomes, metatranscriptomes and consortia in a new area of research for the laboratory. Duties will focus on running new algorithms developed in the group. For more information on past work, please visit the lab website here: ( http://med.stanford.edu/salzmanlab.html ).

The Bioinformatician will work in a highly collaborative environment, carry out data analysis and integration, and apply best-in-class algorithms – or develop new algorithms – that directly address the motivating biological questions. Further, the Bioinformatician will develop reproducible and well-documented analytical pipelines for the analysis of high-throughput data, such as novel analysis of DNA-seq and RNA-seq from metagenomics and transcriptomics. Proficiency in high-throughput genomic data analysis and a good understanding of biological systems are required, as are experience in programming and a solid background in statistical analysis. Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to interact effectively with members of the research teams are essential to the success of the individual in this position. The successful candidate must be able to learn and work independently, yet collaborate effectively with co-workers.

Duties Include

Prioritize and extract data from a variety of sources such as notes, survey results, medical reports, and laboratory data, and maintain its accuracy and completeness.
Determine additional data collection and reporting requirements.
Design and customize reports based upon data in the database.
Oversee and monitor regulatory compliance for utilization of the data.
Use system reports and analyses to identify potentially problematic data, make corrections, and eliminate root cause for data problems or justify solutions to be implemented by others.
Create complex charts and databases, perform statistical analyses, and develop graphs and tables for publication and presentation.
Serve as a resource for non-routine inquiries such as requests for statistics or surveys.
Test prototype software and participate in approval and release process for new software.

The RDA1 will perform analysis/interpretation of genomic data alongside other multi-omic and medical data to facilitate diagnosis of rare genetic disease and will assist in additional aspects of case management for CUD participants. They will also assist in creating and/or managing datasets to facilitate efficient case tracking to ensure participants are moving through the evaluation pipeline efficiently and with all data elements required by the study protocol.

To be successful in this role, you must have a strong background in Mendelian genetics; prior experience with variant interpretation, translational research program, and/or managing research results is an asset. Strong problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills are essential. You will be expected to participate in supporting and tracking participant activities, case management, data analysis, project work, and research workflow. This is a one-year fixed-term position.

This is a hybrid eligible position.

:

Collect, manage and clean datasets.
Employ new and existing tools to interpret, analyze, and visualize multivariate relationships in data.
Create databases and reports, develop algorithms and statistical models, and perform statistical analyses appropriate to data and reporting requirements.
Use system reports and analyses to identify potentially problematic data, make corrections, and determine root cause for data problems from input errors or inadequate field edits, and suggest possible solutions.
Develop reports, charts, graphs and tables for use by investigators and for publication and presentation.
Analyze data processes in documentation.
Collaborate with faculty and research staff on data collection and analysis methods.

Communicate with government officials, grant agencies and industry representatives.

Minimum Experience

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Ability to prioritize workload.

About UMOM New Day Centers:
Founded in 1964, UMOM is Arizona's largest provider of services for families experiencing homelessness. Our mission is to end family homelessness by restoring hope and rebuilding lives. With an annual operating budget of $20 million dollars, UMOM provides shelter, supportive services, and housing programs to families and individuals experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County. UMOM serves over 15,000 unique individuals across all our services annually, including those families receiving support at the Family Housing Hub, Maricopa County's family coordinated entry system.

Position Description:
The SSVF Case Manager is responsible for providing comprehensive, housing-focused case management to Veterans and Veteran families participating in UMOM's Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) program. This position works directly with Veterans to identify and address barriers to housing stability, develop individualized housing and service plans, connect participants with income and community resources, and support participants in obtaining and maintaining permanent housing. The SSVF Case Manager builds strong, respectful relationships with Veterans and collaborates with landlords, community providers, Veteran-serving organizations, and internal teams to coordinate services and promote long-term housing stability.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Client Engagement and Rapport Building

Engage Veterans and Veteran families in a respectful, client-centered manner to build rapport and establish a collaborative case management relationship.
Assess immediate needs, housing barriers, strengths, income, benefits, and other factors impacting housing stability while identifying and strategizing barriers to long-term success.
Orient participants to SSVF program expectations, available services, and applicable resources.
Utilize Trauma Informed Care, Motivational Interviewing, and other evidence-based approaches when providing services.

Collaboration

Work collaboratively with Veterans to develop individualized case plans focused on obtaining and maintaining permanent housing.
Coordinate services with internal UMOM teams and external providers to ensure Veterans receive comprehensive support.
Develop and maintain collaborative relationships with community providers and organizations serving Veterans.
Participate in case staffing and service coordination meetings to identify solutions to participant barriers and strengthen housing stability plans.

Meets regularly and consistently with your client to hold structured, intentional conversations focused on the skill-building necessary to obtain and retain employment/regular income and obtain and retain permanent housing.
Transport and/or accompany clients as needed to support with housing and/or employment search or to make connections to other resources.
Ensures clients exiting to permanent housing are supported with an orientation to the neighborhood and that connections are made with local contacts and resources, inclusive of but not limited to local viable transportation options.
Other duties as assigned by Leadership and/or Executives.
